items.answer: Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.

Hybrid employees assigned to a hub office must work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by the team, not by the individual, to ensure team onsite days overlap and office time is collaborative; most teams anchor on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

The 3-day requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average in MosaicOne rather than week by week, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem. Weeks containing a company holiday, approved PTO or approved travel reduce the requirement proportionally.

Next steps:
- Confirm your team's specific onsite days with your manager
- Review your rolling four-week average in MosaicOne to verify compliance

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

The 401(k) plan has no waiting period; employees may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

Next steps:
- Confirm your hire date to calculate your coverage start date
- Enroll in benefits during week one so elections are in place when eligibility arrives

Mosaic Robotics will never ask an employee for their password, and no genuine internal request will ever ask for a payroll change, a payment redirection or a bulk personal-data extract over email alone. Requests of that shape are verified by a second channel before anyone acts on them, every time, without exception, regardless of who appears to have sent them.

Report suspected phishing by forwarding the message to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example. The security team answers every report, including the ones that turn out to be legitimate mail, and publishes a short monthly summary of what was seen.

Recommendation — not company policy: Do not reply to the message and do not act on the request. The email exhibits multiple phishing signals: a request for bulk personal data over email alone, an external address, and urgency framing. Forward it immediately to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example and delete it.

Next steps:
- Forward the suspicious email to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example
- Delete the message
- Do not send any data or reply to the sender

Each employee may claim up to USD 750 per plan year for home office furniture and accessories. The allowance is intended for items such as a desk, chair, lamp, footrest, adjustable monitor arm, acoustic treatment, or small filing cabinet.

The allowance resets on 1 January and does not carry over year to year.

Laptops, monitors, docks, keyboards, mice, headsets and webcams are not claimed against this allowance; they are issued as company assets under the Equipment & Asset Policy.

Next steps:
- Review the full home office allowance policy section for eligibility details based on your work arrangement (remote, hybrid, or onsite)
- Submit claims in MosaicOne Expenses with clear descriptions of items purchased

Mosaic Robotics provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to every eligible new parent. The 16 weeks are the same whether the employee gave birth, did not give birth, adopted, or became a parent through surrogacy or foster placement leading to adoption.

Next steps:
- Confirm your eligibility (6 months of continuous service required)
- Contact People Operations to discuss timing and any splitting of leave into up to three blocks

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates.

Where the cap cannot be met, the traveller books the most reasonable available option and notes the reason. No pre-approval is needed.

Next steps:
- Contact MosaicOne Travel if you need clarification on whether your destination qualifies for the higher cap or if you encounter a market where the standard cap cannot be met.

International remote work of more than 30 consecutive days requires approval from the employee's director and from Tax & Legal before travel begins.

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review to determine whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether the employee's planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure and must name the destination, exact dates, workspace address, and a description of the work to be performed.

The employee must hold the right to work in the destination country, meet device and connectivity requirements, and stay inside the company's rolling 90-day annual limit.

Manager approval, director approval, and Tax & Legal approval are three separate records and all three must be present before departure.

Next steps:
- Submit Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne at least 21 calendar days before departure
- Obtain director approval in addition to direct manager approval
- Await Tax & Legal determination of shadow payroll, certificate of coverage, and permanent-establishment exposure

Flights must be booked at least 14 calendar days before departure whenever the itinerary is known.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of USD 25 or more.

Expense reports of USD 2,501 to USD 10,000 require director approval and a finance business partner as second approver.

Next steps:
- Book the conference trip through MosaicOne Travel at least 14 days before departure
- Obtain manager approval before booking, then director approval for the USD 3,000 spend
- Retain itemised receipts for all expenses of USD 25 or more
- Submit the expense report with director and finance business partner approval

Security and acceptable-use training must be completed within 14 calendar days of the start date.

Benefits enrolment opens in week one, and coverage begins at the end of the 90-day waiting period. The 401(k) has no waiting period, so a new hire may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

IT ships standard equipment to arrive at least 5 business days before the start date. The shipment contains the laptop, adapter, headset and, for remote hires, the monitor, keyboard, mouse and dock.

Payroll setup, tax withholding elections and 401(k) enrolment are completed in week one.

Next steps:
- Confirm your start date with your hiring manager to ensure equipment arrives on schedule
- Complete identity verification and acceptable-use acknowledgement on day one
- Attend the benefits question session (held every second Tuesday) if you need guidance on elections

Severity 1 cases receive a response within 4 business hours. Response means a named human being contacting the person who raised the case, acknowledging what was raised, naming who owns it and describing what happens next.

Target resolution times are as fast as the facts allow for Severity 1 cases. Where a case will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update. Updates continue at least every 10 business days until the case closes.

Escalation: The published policy does not specify a separate investigation timeline or investigation completion deadline for Severity 1 cases. Contact People Operations for details on investigation procedures and expected duration.

Next steps:
- Confirm the case reference number when you receive the initial response
- Request a written update if the case extends beyond the initial response
- Contact People Operations if you need clarification on investigation status

As of 2026-09-01, you have 13.5 remaining PTO days.

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

PTO requests of any length are approved by your direct manager. Requests of 6 to 15 consecutive business days require 15 business days' notice; requests of more than 15 consecutive business days require director approval in addition to manager approval and 15 business days' notice. Requests overlapping a declared blackout period require director approval and 5 business days' notice.

Next steps:
- Determine the length and dates of your intended PTO request
- Submit your request in MosaicOne with appropriate advance notice based on request length
- Obtain manager approval; director approval if request exceeds 15 consecutive business days or overlaps blackout dates (2026-12-22 or 2026-12-23)

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne. Verbal agreement, a message in chat and an email thread are all insufficient on their own: the approval must be recorded against the request so the audit trail is complete.

PTO requests of any length are approved by the employee's direct manager.

Recommendation — not company policy: You have 13.5 PTO days remaining as of 2026-09-01. Your three-day request is covered by your balance. Submit your request in MosaicOne at least 5 business days before Tuesday 15 September (by Tuesday 8 September at the latest) to allow your manager time to approve it in writing.

Next steps:
- Calculate your submission deadline: 5 business days before 15 September 2026 is 8 September 2026.
- Submit the PTO request in MosaicOne with the dates 15–17 September 2026.
- Obtain written manager approval in MosaicOne before the first day of your absence.

You meet the tenure requirement: employees must have completed at least 12 months of continuous service to work outside their home country. Your tenure as of 2026-09-01 is 45 months.

Germany is an approved destination for temporary work abroad.

Your proposed stay of 42 consecutive days (3 November to 14 December, inclusive) exceeds the 30-day threshold and therefore requires Tax & Legal review before travel begins, director approval (not just manager approval), and a Tax & Legal review request filed at least 21 calendar days before departure.

No employee may work outside their home country for more than 90 days in a rolling 12-month period. Your 42-day stay falls within this limit.

Work performed outside your home country must use a company-managed, full-disk-encrypted laptop with always-on VPN. Personal devices may not be used for any Mosaic Robotics work outside your home country.

Recommendation — not company policy: You have approximately 63 days until 3 November 2026. Raise your request in MosaicOne under 'Work from another country' immediately, naming the destination (Berlin), exact dates (3 November to 14 December), and workspace address. File the Tax & Legal review request at least 21 calendar days before departure. Notify IT Security of the destination at least 5 business days before departure and confirm your laptop meets the encryption and VPN requirements.

Escalation: Contact People Operations at mobility@mosaicrobotics.example to file the Tax & Legal review request and coordinate director approval. The review will determine whether shadow payroll, social security coverage, or permanent-establishment mitigation is required.

Next steps:
- Raise the request in MosaicOne under 'Work from another country' with exact dates and Berlin workspace address.
- File a Tax & Legal review request at least 21 calendar days before departure (by approximately 13 October 2026).
- Obtain director approval from Dana (your director) and Tax & Legal approval before travel.
- Notify IT Security of Germany as destination at least 5 business days before departure.
- Confirm your laptop is company-managed, full-disk-encrypted, and configured with always-on VPN.

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

Your 90-day waiting period ends on 2026-11-13, at which point your coverage begins.

You have 30 days from the end of the waiting period to make elections in MosaicOne Benefits. If you make no election within that window, you will be enrolled in employee-only coverage on the standard medical plan by default.

Benefits enrollment opens in week one even though coverage does not begin until the 90-day waiting period ends, so you can make your elections in advance.

Next steps:
- Log into MosaicOne Benefits to review and make your coverage elections before 2026-11-13
- Attend a benefits question session (held every second Tuesday) if you have questions about your options
- Confirm your elections are submitted by 2026-12-13 (30 days after your waiting period ends)
